changes: Open multiple files or a folder in one selection, preserving nested folders
Skip unsupported and hidden files, retain successful imports, and retry only known pre-creation failures
Select multiple library documents and open them together in application tabs
Retain open documents and pending edits across tab switches with account-scoped caches
Open a single comment beside its passage or browse all comment conversations
Preserve unread state until the displayed conversation is read
Retain rejected local edits and show their save failure after switching tabs

api.note: This release changes the web app and uses the existing folders, document import, live sync, comments and thread-read APIs.

validation.static_checks_evidence: pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test, and isolated production build exited 0 for the committed source revision.

native_folder_picker.reason: The browser automation directory chooser call returned without populating selected files. The directory selection step was not demonstrated end to end.
native_folder_picker.separate_verified_evidence: The native multiple-file UI worked. The exact import planner and runner imported the directory fixture through the real local API: four Markdown files, two skipped files, and three folders with hierarchy and content verified.

checks: Homepage shows Open files and Open folder controls
Select all selects two existing documents; Open selected creates both tabs
Both tabs render their own document and switch back successfully
Profile-photo marker opens exactly one thread card beside the passage
All comments displays both production thread cards

limitations: Native directory selection has not been fully verified through the browser tool; directory planning, creation, hierarchy and content were verified separately against the local API.
Ambiguous network or server failures are not automatically retried because the import endpoints do not support idempotency; confirmed successful docs remain available.
The standalone Playwright suite was not rerun; browser validation used CUA in the requested Chrome session.
